```{r funtions,message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Create a discrete scale function
my_scale_colour <- function(...) {
  ggplot2::discrete_scale(
    domain = ggplot2::domain(),
    range = my_palette$primary,
    ...
  )
}

plot_standard_ests<-function(df,title,ylab,xlab,col_pallete){
  
  df$Estimate.P_clean<-round(df$Estimate.P, digits = 1)
  
  plot<-ggplot2::ggplot(df, aes(x=factor(df$Subpopulation), y=df$Estimate.P,alpha = 0.5)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity",aes(fill=df$Subpopulation)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_pallete)+
  geom_crossbar( aes(x=factor(df$Subpopulation), y=df$Estimate.P, ymin=df$LCB95Pct.P, ymax=df$UCB95Pct.P), colour="grey", alpha=0.5, size=0.5, fill = "grey")+
  # ggpattern::geom_crossbar_pattern( aes(x=factor(chloride_ests$Category), y=chloride_ests$Estimate.P, ymin=chloride_ests$LCB95Pct.P, ymax=chloride_ests$UCB95Pct.P), size = 0.5)+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin= df$LCB95Pct.P,
                    ymax= df$UCB95Pct.P),
                width=.2,                    # Width of the error bars
                position="identity",
                alpha = 0.1)+
geom_text(aes(label = paste(Estimate.P_clean,"%",sep = "")), position = position_dodge(width = 1),vjust = -0.1)+
  coord_flip()+ggtitle(label = title)+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot+facet_wrap(~Category) + ylab(ylab)+xlab(xlab)

}

#relative risk
risk_spsurvey<-function(df,stressor,response){
  risk_df<-df
  
  risk_df<-risk_df |> 
    filter(stressor != "no_sample")
  
  #run the survey
  relrisk_list<-spsurvey::relrisk_analysis(risk_df,
  vars_response = response,
  vars_stressor = stressor, 
  siteID = "SITE_CODE",
  weight = "final_weight",
  xcoord = "LONGITUDE",
  ycoord = "LATITUDE")
  
}

#attributable risk
#write a function to do this
attrib_risk_spsurvey<-function(df,stressor,response){
  risk_df<-df
  
  risk_df<-risk_df |> 
    filter(response != "no_sample") |> 
    filter(stressor != "no_sample")
  
  #run the survey
  relrisk_list<-spsurvey::attrisk_analysis(risk_df,
  vars_response = response,
  vars_stressor = stressor, 
  siteID = "SITE_CODE",
  weight = "final_weight",
  xcoord = "LONGITUDE",
  ycoord = "LATITUDE")
  
}

#function to plot them

plot_cat_analysis<-function(df,param,col_pallete){
 
  df$Estimate.P_clean<-round(df$Estimate.P, digits = 1)
  
plot<-ggplot2::ggplot(df, aes(fill=Category, y=Estimate.P, x = Subpopulation)) +
  geom_bar(position='dodge', stat='identity',alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_palette_d(col_pallete)+
  geom_crossbar(aes(x=Subpopulation, y=Estimate.P, ymin=LCB95Pct.P, ymax=UCB95Pct.P,group = Category),
                colour="grey", alpha=0.5,
                width = 0.9,
                linewidth = 0.1,
                fill = "grey",
                position = position_dodge(0.9))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin= LCB95Pct.P,
                    ymax= UCB95Pct.P),
                width=.2,                    # Width of the error bars
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
                alpha = 0.1)+
geom_text(aes(label = paste(Estimate.P_clean,"%",sep = "")), position = position_dodge(width = 1),hjust = -0.1)+
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.10)))+
  coord_flip()+ggtitle(label = paste(stringr::str_to_title(param),sep = " "))+
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  # scale_x_discrete(limits = rev)+
  labs(y = "Estimated % of Lakes in NYS",
       x = "Sample Type")+
  theme_light()+
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
plot
}
```

## reweigh the design

```{r reweight_the_design, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}


#create a use vector for if it was used or not
used_site<-function(df){   
  df<-df %>% 
    mutate(use=case_when(EvalStatus %in% c("TS") ~TRUE, #this is a notation for "target sample"
                         TRUE~FALSE))
} #if it was dry note that and do not use the TS - ONLY use TS if we sampled it


#create the true/false column needed to adjust the weights
prob_1<-used_site(df = wgts_merge3) #this will be the dataframe from above with the EvalStatus notes - 

#create function to adjust the weights
adjust_weight<-function(df,caty_number){
  n = caty_number 
 
  # # or pre-allocate for slightly more efficiency
  datalist = vector("list", length = n) # n of the categories
  # 
  framesize_x<-df %>% 
    group_by(caty) |> #group by the category
    dplyr::summarise(n=sum(wgt)) #this should be the sum of each category - this is a sum to the statewide frame - not by strata
    for (i in framesize_x$caty){#for 26-27{
    print(i)
    df2<-df |> 
      filter(caty %in% i)#for 26-27
    
    
    wgt<-df2$wgt
    wgtcat<-df2$caty
    
    sites<-df2$use
    
    framesize_y<-framesize_x |> 
      filter(caty %in% i) #for 26-27

    x1<-framesize_y$caty #for 26-27
    
    x2<-framesize_y$n
    framesize<-setNames(x2,x1)
    
    x<-spsurvey::adjwgt(wgt,wgtcat,framesize,sites) 
    
    df_adj<-cbind(df2,x) 
    df_adj<-df_adj |> select(wgt, final_weight = x,caty,caty,everything())
    datalist[[i]] <- df_adj # add it to your list
  }
  
  big_data = do.call(rbind, datalist)
}

prob_1_adjusted<-adjust_weight(prob_1,4) #for 4 lake size categories


final_site_list<-prob_1_adjusted |> 
  filter(EvalStatus %in% "TS") |> 
  distinct()

sites_wgts<-final_site_list |> 
  select(LOCATION_ID,Lake,final_weight,lat_WGS84,lon_WGS84) |> 
  distinct() |> 
  rename(SITE_CODE = LOCATION_ID)

```

```{r mising-eurofins-data}

library(readxl)
folder_path <- here::here("data/missing_eurofins_data")

xls_files <- list.files(path = folder_path, pattern = "\\.xls$", full.names = TRUE)

# Read all files and combine into one data frame
missing_euro <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(xls_files, function(file) {
    tryCatch({
      # Read first sheet; adjust 'sheet' if needed
      df <- readxl::read_excel(file, sheet = 1)
      df$SourceFile <- basename(file)  # Add column to track source
      df
    }, error = function(e) {
      warning(sprintf("Error reading file %s: %s", file, e$message))
      NULL
    })
  }))


#format to add in

missing_euro_fix<-missing_euro |> 
  filter(`Sample Type` %in% 'Field Sample') |> 
  select(SAMPLE_NAME =`Client ID`,
         EVENT_DATETIME = Collected,
         RESULT_VALUE = Result,
         RESULT_QUALIFIER = `Result Flag`,
         UNIT = Units,
         PARAMETER_NAME = Analyte,
         MRL
         ) |> 
  mutate(SAMPLE_NAME = substr(SAMPLE_NAME, nchar(SAMPLE_NAME) - 7, nchar(SAMPLE_NAME))) |> 
  #Fix wrong sample key from lab
  mutate(SAMPLE_NAME = case_when(
    SAMPLE_NAME %in% "25L0383" ~ "25L0384",
    str_detect(SAMPLE_NAME, "25S") ~ str_replace_all(SAMPLE_NAME, "25S", "25L"),
    .default = SAMPLE_NAME
  )) |> 
  #Set result values to NA when qualifier = "<"
  mutate(RESULT_VALUE = case_when(
    RESULT_QUALIFIER == "<" ~ NA,
    .default = RESULT_VALUE
  )) |> 
  mutate(RESULT_QUALIFIER = case_when(
    RESULT_QUALIFIER == "=" ~ "A",
    RESULT_QUALIFIER == "<" ~ "U",
    .default = RESULT_QUALIFIER
  ))

#bring in the lake ids for these -
```

## Cat analysis - run spsurvey

```{r toxins-spsurvey,message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

parameter_list<-c("anatoxin_a",                                       "cylindrospermopsin",                                  
"microcystin_la",                                      
 "microcystin_lf",                                      
 "microcystin_lr",                                      
 "microcystin_ly" ,                                     
 "microcystin_rr" ,                                     
 "microcystin_yr" ,                                     
 "nodularin",
"microcystin")


toxins_spsurvey<-toxins2 |> 
  mutate(RESULT_VALUE = as.numeric(RESULT_VALUE)) |> 
  mutate(RESULT_VALUE = case_when(str_detect(RESULT_QUALIFIER, "U")~ 0,
                                  TRUE ~ RESULT_VALUE)) |> 
  mutate(present = case_when(RESULT_VALUE > 0 ~ "present",
                             TRUE ~ "non-detect" )) |> 
  filter(SAMPLE_METHOD %in% c("integrated_disturbance_sample", "scrape", "floating_mat"))


# Complete the dataset - so there is aline for each parameter and each method
df_completed <- toxins_spsurvey |> 
  tidyr::complete(
    SITE_CODE      = unique(toxins_spsurvey$SITE_CODE),
    SAMPLE_METHOD    = c("integrated_disturbance_sample", "scrape", "floating_mat"),
    PARAMETER_NAME = parameter_list,
    fill      = list(RESULT_VALUE = as.numeric(NA)  # or "not sampled" if it's text
  )) |> 
  mutate(present = case_when(SAMPLE_METHOD %in% "floating_mat" & is.na(RESULT_VALUE)~"not_sampled",
                             TRUE ~ present)) |> 
  select(-c(SAMPLE_LATITUDE,SAMPLE_LONGITUDE,final_weight))

#get the lat/longs back
locations<-toxins_spsurvey |> 
  select(SITE_CODE,SAMPLE_LATITUDE,SAMPLE_LONGITUDE,final_weight) |> 
  unique()

df_completed2<-df_completed |> 
  left_join(locations,
            by = "SITE_CODE") |> 
  mutate(SAMPLE_METHOD = case_when(
    SAMPLE_METHOD %in% "integrated_disturbance_sample" ~ "IDS",
    TRUE ~ SAMPLE_METHOD
  ))
```

#NYS thresholds

```{r}
#first create the categories - above the thresholds, below or not sampled mc is 4 ug/l (NYS), cylindro is 15 ug/l (EPA)
toxins_nys_thresholds<-toxins.sf |> #first put the non-detects to 0 so they get sorted
  filter(PARAMETER_NAME %in% c("microcystin","cylindrospermopsin")) |> 
  mutate(nys_threshold_m = case_when(
    (PARAMETER_NAME %in% "microcystin" & RESULT_VALUE > 4)~"above",
    (PARAMETER_NAME %in% "microcystin" & RESULT_VALUE <= 4) ~ "below",
     (PARAMETER_NAME %in% "microcystin" & RESULT_QUALIFIER %in% "U") ~ "below",
    TRUE~"not_sampled"),
    nys_threshold_c =  case_when(
    (PARAMETER_NAME %in% "cylindrospermopsin" & RESULT_VALUE > 15)~"above",
    (PARAMETER_NAME %in% "cylindrospermopsin" & RESULT_VALUE <= 15) ~ "below",
    (PARAMETER_NAME %in% "cylindrospermopsin" & RESULT_QUALIFIER %in% "U") ~ "below",
    TRUE~"not_sampled"))

#filter to the correct parameters
thresh_m_df<-toxins_nys_thresholds |> 
  filter(PARAMETER_NAME %in% "microcystin")

thresh_c_df<-toxins_nys_thresholds |> 
  filter(PARAMETER_NAME %in% "cylindrospermopsin")


  #run the spsurvey data
cat_thresh_m<-standard_ests<-spsurvey::cat_analysis(
  dframe = thresh_m_df,
  vars = "nys_threshold_m",
  subpops = "SAMPLE_METHOD",
  siteID = "SITE_CODE",
  weight = "final_weight"
)

 #run the spsurvey data
cat_thresh_c<-standard_ests<-spsurvey::cat_analysis(
  dframe = thresh_c_df,
  vars = "nys_threshold_c",
  subpops = "SAMPLE_METHOD",
  siteID = "SITE_CODE",
  weight = "final_weight"
)

#filter out the "total" category

cat_thresh_m<-cat_thresh_m |> 
  filter(Category !="Total")
cat_thresh_c<-cat_thresh_c |> 
  filter(Category !="Total")

#plot them
thresh_m_plot<- plot_cat_analysis(df = cat_thresh_m,
                                  param = NULL,
                                  col_pallete = my_palette4_thresh$primary)&
   theme(legend.position = "bottom", # Moves the legend to the bottom
         legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
         legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
           axis.text = element_text(size = 14))& 
        labs(fill = "NYS Recreational Threshold\n Total Microcystins (4 µg/l)") # chnages the main title
thresh_m_plot

#plot them
thresh_c_plot<- plot_cat_analysis(df = cat_thresh_c,
                                  param = "cylindrospermopsin",
                                  col_pallete = my_p1_thresh$primary)&
   theme(legend.position = "bottom",
         legend.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
         legend.text = element_text(size = 14)) # Moves the legend to the bottom
```

## Map of sites with toxin detection status

```{r toxins-all-map ,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}

lakes_with_cyanos3<-lakes_with_cyanos2 |> 
  select(SITE_CODE, toxigenic_present) |> 
  filter(toxigenic_present %in% "toxigenic_present")

toxins_map <- toxins2 %>%
  filter(PARAMETER_NAME %in% parameter_list) |> 
  group_by(SITE_CODE) %>%
  summarize(
    any_detect = if_else(any(!is.na(RESULT_VALUE)), "Yes", "No")
  ) |> 
  left_join(lakes_with_cyanos3) |> 
  rename(cyano_present = toxigenic_present) |> 
  mutate(cyano_present = case_when(
    is.na(cyano_present) ~ "No",
    cyano_present %in% "toxigenic_present" ~ "Yes",
  )) |> 
  distinct(SITE_CODE, any_detect, cyano_present)


site_locations<-toxins2 |> 
  select(SITE_CODE, SAMPLE_LATITUDE, SAMPLE_LONGITUDE) |> 
  distinct() |> 
  left_join(toxins_map) |> 
  na.omit()

nys_major_drainage_basins<- st_read("L:/DOW/BWAM Share/data/gis/nys_major_drainage_basins/nys_major_drainage_basins.shp")

site_locations_points <- st_as_sf(site_locations, coords = c("SAMPLE_LONGITUDE", "SAMPLE_LATITUDE"), crs = 4326)

# Define the target CRS (replace 'EPSG:4326' with your desired CRS)
target_crs <- st_crs("EPSG:26918")

# Transform the polygon layer to the target CRS
site_locations_points <- st_transform(site_locations_points, target_crs)

site_locations_points <- site_locations_points |>
  mutate(any_detect = factor(any_detect, levels = c("Yes", "No"))) |> 
  mutate(cyano_present = factor(cyano_present, levels = c("Yes", "No")))

ggplot() +
  # Layer 1: Plot the NYS background map
  geom_sf(data = nys_major_drainage_basins, fill = "white", color = "gray60") +
  
  # Layer 2: Plot the lake points and map the "yes_no_field" to color
  # Note: Replace 'yes_no_field' with the exact name of your column
  geom_sf(data = site_locations_points, aes(color = as.factor(any_detect), shape = cyano_present), size = 2.5) +
  
  # Layer 3: Customize the categorical colors manually
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Yes" = "#FACE00", "No" = "#154973"), # Custom Hex codes for your values
    breaks = c("Yes", "No"),
    name = "Toxins Detected"                         # Title for your map legend
  ) +
 scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Cyanos Present",
    values = c("Yes" = 16, "No" = 17), # 16 = Filled Circle, 17 = Filled Triangle
    breaks = c("Yes", "No"),
  ) +
  
  # Layer 4: Formatting and clean presentation layout
  theme(
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),    # Removes grid lines
    axis.text = element_blank(),     # Removes lat/long text labels
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),    # Removes tick marks
    axis.title = element_blank(),    # Removes axis titles (Lat/Long)
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "gray75", color = NA), # Map interior
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "gray75", color = NA),   # Map margins
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray75", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
  )+
  # Add the scale bar
  annotation_scale(
    location = "bl",       # "bl" = bottom left
    width_hint = 0.3,      # Approx proportion of the map width to occupy
    unit_category = "metric" # Uses km/m (use "imperial" for mi/ft)
  ) +
  
  # Add the north arrow
  annotation_north_arrow(
    location = "tr",       # "tr" = top right
    which_north = "true",  # Adjusts for the map projection
    pad_x = unit(0.4, "in"), 
    pad_y = unit(0.4, "in"), # Space padding from the edge
    style = north_arrow_fancy_orienteering
```

## Extent - Impacted Categories

```{r message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

spl_categories<-lake_df |>
  mutate(WATERBODY_CODE = paste(SITE_CODE,"_DH",sep = "")) |> 
  filter(PARAMETER_NAME %in% c(
                               "iron",
                               "nitrogen",
                               "ph",
                               "phosphorus",
                               "secchi_disk_depth",
                               "sulfate",
                               "chlorophyll-a"
                               )) |> 
  mutate(parameter_full = paste(PARAMETER_NAME,UNIT,sep = "_")) |>
  filter(parameter_full != "chlorophyll-a_RFU") |> 
  select(-c(PROJECT,PARAMETER_NAME,UNIT, FRACTION,EVENT_ID,RESULT_QUALIFIER)) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = parameter_full,
                     values_from = RESULT_VALUE,
                     values_fn = function(x) median(x,na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(phos_cat = case_when(
    `phosphorus_mg/L` > 0.020 ~ "impacted",
    is.na(`phosphorus_mg/L`)~ "no_sample",
    TRUE~ "non-impacted")) |> 
  mutate(iron_cat = case_when(
    `iron_ug/L` > 2000 ~ "impacted",
    is.na(`iron_ug/L`)~ "no_sample",
    TRUE ~ "non-impacted")) |> 
  mutate(nitrogen_cat = case_when(
    `nitrogen_ug/L` >= 600 ~"impacted",
    `nitrogen_ug/L` < 600 ~ "non-impacted",
    TRUE ~ "no_sample")) |> 
      mutate(ph_cat = case_when(
        (`ph_pH units` > 8.5 | `ph_pH units` < 6.5) ~ "impacted",
        (`ph_pH units`>= 6.6 & `ph_pH units` < 8.5) ~ "non-impacted",
        TRUE ~ "no_sample")) |> 
   mutate(secchi_cat = case_when(
        (`secchi_disk_depth_meters` > 2) ~ "non-impacted",
        (`secchi_disk_depth_meters` <= 2) ~ "impacted",
        TRUE ~ "no_sample")) |>
       mutate(sulf_cat = case_when(
        (`sulfate_ug/L` > 300) ~ "impacted",
        (`sulfate_ug/L` <= 300) ~ "non-impacted",
        TRUE ~ "no_sample")) |> 
mutate(np_ratio = ((`nitrogen_ug/L`/1000)/14.007)/((`phosphorus_mg/L`)/30.974)) |> #convert to mg/L and then get moles of N / moles P
  mutate(np_cat = case_when(
    np_ratio <=15 ~ "impacted",
    np_ratio >15 ~"non-impacted",
    TRUE~ "no_sample"
  )) |> 
    mutate(chla_cat = case_when(
    `chlorophyll-a_ug/L` >8 ~ "impacted",
    `chlorophyll-a_ug/L` <=8 ~"non-impacted",
    TRUE~ "no_sample"
  ))

#merge with phab and scale metrics

spl_categories<-spl_categories |> 
  left_join(phab_all,by = "SITE_CODE") |> 
  left_join(scale_all,by = "SITE_CODE") |> #create the groups for canopy cover
  mutate(canopy_cat = case_when(
    canopy_average <= 25 ~ "impacted",
    canopy_average > 25 ~ "non-impacted",
    TRUE ~ "no_sample"))
#merge with the toxins
#need to get the toxins in here - maybe per lake AND per sample type? not sure yet
# could have a column for each type of sample and the present/absent

toxins_short<-toxins.sf |> 
  select(SITE_CODE,EVENT_DATETIME,SAMPLE_METHOD,
         present) |> 
  filter(present %in% "present") |> 
  distinct() #why are there repeats? figure out why there are some with method populated twice - its because there are multiple toxins!

spl_categories<-spl_categories |> 
  mutate(toxins_present = case_when(
    SITE_CODE %in% toxins_short$SITE_CODE ~ "present",
    TRUE ~ "non-detect"
  ))

#get the weights back in
spl_categories<-spl_categories |> 
  left_join(sites_wgts, by = "SITE_CODE")

spl_categories<-spl_categories |> 
  filter(final_weight > 0)


#create sf object
spl_categories <- sf::st_as_sf(spl_categories,
  coords = c("LONGITUDE", "LATITUDE"),
  crs = "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs"
)


```

## RElative Risk

RR \> 1: The stressor increases the likelihood of poor condition.

RR = 1: No association.

RR \< 1: The stressor is associated with better condition.

```{r relative-risk-start}
#use the same as above but it needs to say poor or good
spl_categories2<-spl_categories |> 
    mutate(across(
    .cols = c("phos_cat",
              "iron_cat",
              "nitrogen_cat",
              "ph_cat",
              "secchi_cat",
              "canopy_cat",
              "sulf_cat",
              "np_cat",
              "chla_cat"
              ),  # columns to modify
    .fns = ~ ifelse(. == "impacted", "Poor", .)  # replacement logic
  )) |> 
    mutate(across(
    .cols = c("phos_cat",
              "iron_cat",
              "nitrogen_cat",
              "ph_cat",
              "secchi_cat",
              "canopy_cat",
              "sulf_cat",
              "np_cat",
              "chla_cat"),  # columns to modify
    .fns = ~ ifelse(. == "non-impacted", "Good", .)  # replacement logic
  )) |> 
  mutate(toxins_present = case_when(
    toxins_present %in% "present" ~ "Poor",
    toxins_present %in% "non-detect" ~ "Good",
    TRUE ~ "no_sample"
  ))

#run them! with the function above

phos_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2, 
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "phos_cat")
iron_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2, 
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "iron_cat")
ph_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2, 
                       response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "ph_cat")
secchi_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2, 
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "secchi_cat")
canopy_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2, 
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "canopy_cat")
nitrogen_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "nitrogen_cat")
chla_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "chla_cat")
# np_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
#                         response = "toxins_present",
#                         stressor = "np_cat") #cant do this one either bc they're all good
# np_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
#                         response = "toxins_present",
#                         stressor = "np_cat")
# 
# sulf_risk<-risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
#                         response = "toxins_present",
#                         stressor = "sulf_cat") #cant do this one bc we dont have any in the "good" category
#doesnt have all of the categories

risk_all <- rbind(phos_risk,
                  iron_risk,
                  ph_risk,
                  secchi_risk,
                  canopy_risk,
                  chla_risk,
                  nitrogen_risk)

risk_all<-risk_all |> 
    mutate(Stressor = factor(Stressor, levels = c("phos_cat",
                                                  "nitrogen_cat",
                                                  "np_cat",
                                                  "chla_cat",
                                                  "sulf_cat",
                                                  "iron_cat",
                                                  "ph_cat",
                                                  "secchi_cat",
                                                  "canopy_cat"))) |> 
    group_by(Stressor) |> 
  mutate(Estimate_clean = round(Estimate, digits = 1))

risk_all$Stressor<-dplyr::recode(risk_all$Stressor,
                                                "phos_cat" = "Total Phosphate",
                                               "nitrogen_cat" = "Total Nitrogen",
                                               "ph_cat" = "pH",
                                               "chla_cat" = "Chlorophyl A",
                                               "sulf_cat" = "Sulfate",
                                               "iron_cat"= "Iron",
                                               "secchi_cat" = "Secchi",
                                               "canopy_cat" = "Canopy",
                                               "np_cat" = "NP Ratio")
#plot them!!

plot_risk<-risk_all |> 
  ggplot2::ggplot(aes(x=Stressor,
                                         y=Estimate)) +
  geom_point(stat="identity",fill ="#233F2B") +
  geom_crossbar( aes(x=Stressor, y=Estimate, ymin=LCB95Pct, ymax=UCB95Pct), colour="grey", alpha=0.1, size=0.5, fill = "grey")+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin= LCB95Pct,
                    ymax= UCB95Pct),
                width=.2,                    # Width of the error bars
                position="identity",
                alpha = 0.09)+
  geom_text(aes(label = Estimate_clean, vjust = -0.1))+
  coord_flip()+ggtitle(label = "Relative Risk")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  labs(y = "Relative Risk Factor",
       x = "")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "#FACE00", width = 0.1)+
  theme_minimal()
plot_risk

```

## Attributable Risk

Attributable risk values close to zero indicate that removing the stressor variable will have little or no impact on the probability that the response variable is in poor condition. Attributable risk values close to one indicate that removing the stressor variable will result in extensive reduction of the probability that the response variable is in poor condition. https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/spsurvey/html/attrisk_analysis.html

```{r}

phos_attrib_risk<-attrib_risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "phos_cat")

iron_attrib_risk<-attrib_risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "iron_cat")
nitrogen_attrib_risk<-attrib_risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "nitrogen_cat")
ph_attrib_risk<-attrib_risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "ph_cat")
secchi_attrib_risk<-attrib_risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "secchi_cat")
canopy_attrib_risk<-attrib_risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "canopy_cat")
chla_attrib_risk<-attrib_risk_spsurvey(df = spl_categories2,
                        response = "toxins_present",
                        stressor = "chla_cat")


attrib_risk_all<-rbind(
  phos_attrib_risk,
  nitrogen_attrib_risk, #epty bc we dont have any in the poor category
  ph_attrib_risk,
  secchi_attrib_risk,
  canopy_attrib_risk,
  iron_attrib_risk,
  chla_attrib_risk)


attrib_risk_all<-attrib_risk_all |> 
    mutate(Stressor = factor(Stressor, levels = c("phos_cat",
                                                  "nitrogen_cat",
                                                  "np_cat",
                                                  "chla_cat",
                                                  "sulf_cat",
                                                  "iron_cat",
                                                  "ph_cat",
                                                  "secchi_cat",
                                                  "canopy_cat"))) |> 
    group_by(Stressor) |> 
  mutate(Estimate_clean = round(Estimate*100, digits = 1))

attrib_risk_all$Stressor<-dplyr::recode(attrib_risk_all$Stressor,
                                              "phos_cat" = "Total Phosphate",
                                               "nitrogen_cat" = "Total Nitrogen",
                                               "ph_cat" = "pH",
                                               "chla_cat" = "Chlorophyl A",
                                               "sulf_cat" = "Sulfate",
                                               "iron_cat"= "Iron",
                                               "secchi_cat" = "Secchi",
                                               "canopy_cat" = "Canopy",
                                               "np_cat" = "NP Ratio")

plot_attrib_risk<-attrib_risk_all |> 
  ggplot2::ggplot(aes(x=Stressor,y=Estimate*100)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity",fill ="#233F2B") +
  geom_crossbar( aes(x=Stressor, y=Estimate *100, ymin=LCB95Pct*100, ymax=UCB95Pct*100), colour="grey", alpha=0.5, size=0.5, fill = "grey")+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin= LCB95Pct,
                    ymax= UCB95Pct),
                width=.2,                    # Width of the error bars
                position="identity",
                alpha = 0.5)+
  geom_text(aes(label = paste(Estimate_clean,"%",sep = ""), vjust = -0.1))+
  coord_flip()+ggtitle(label = "Attributable Risk")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  labs(y = "Attributable Risk",
       x = "")+
  theme_minimal()
plot_attrib_risk


```

RR tells you the strength of the association.

AR tells you the magnitude of impact in terms of cases that could be prevented if the stressor were removed. In spsurvey’s risk analysis vignettes, RR is plotted to show the association, and AR is calculated to show the potential improvement in biological condition if the stressor is reduced

[![](RR_AR_Fig.png)](https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/relative-extent-relative-risk-and-attributable-risk)

```{r water chem and phab distributions any detections}
      ) ~ scale_y_log10(
          labels = scales::label_comma(),
          guide = "axis_logticks" 
        ),
      
      # FOR LINEAR PANELS: Standard continuous scale remains completely clean
      TRUE ~ scale_y_continuous()
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Toxins Detected",
    y = "Result Value"
    #title = "Parameter Distributions by Detect Status"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    
    # FIX: Increase the font size and styling of the legend text
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12), # Makes "Toxins Detected" larger
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),                 # Makes "Yes" / "No" larger
    legend.key.size = unit(1.5, "lines"),                  # Makes the colored boxes larger
    
    # FIX: Bold and scale up the facet header titles
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),   # Bolds parameter titles
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"),      # Optional: subtle background tint
    
    # Controls the length/sizing of the log ticks cleanly via the theme
    axis.ticks.length.y = unit(0.2, "cm") 
  )
```

### Drivers Principal Component Analysis

```{r, PCA}

df_wide <- drivers %>%
  select(SITE_CODE, any_detect, cyano_present, PARAMETER_NAME, RESULT_VALUE) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = PARAMETER_NAME, values_from = RESULT_VALUE) %>%
  drop_na() |>  # Removes missing values since PCA requires a complete matrix
  rename(
  # "TKN" = "kjeldahl_nitrogen",
  # "chl-a" = "chlorophyll-a",
  # "TP" = "total_phosphorus",
  # "DP" = "dissolved_phosphorus",
  "canopy_cover" = "canopy_densiometer_percent",
  "shoreline_disturbance" = "rdis_ix",
  "littoral_habitat_index" = "litcvrqc3oe",
  "riparian_habitat_index" = "rvegqc3oe"
  )

pca_meta <- df_wide %>% select(SITE_CODE, any_detect, cyano_present)
pca_data <- df_wide %>% select(-SITE_CODE, -any_detect, -cyano_present)

# 2. Run PCA with scale and center enabled
pca_results <- prcomp(pca_data, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# 3. Extract PCA Coordinates for data points
df_pca_plot <- as.data.frame(pca_results$x) %>%
  bind_cols(pca_meta)

# 4. Extract and scale the Loadings (Arrows)
# We multiply by a scaling factor so the arrows stretch cleanly across the data space
arrow_scale_factor <- max(abs(df_pca_plot$PC1)) / max(abs(pca_results$rotation[,1])) * 0.7

df_loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_results$rotation) %>%
  mutate(
    parameter = rownames(.),
    x_end = PC1 * arrow_scale_factor,
    y_end = PC2 * arrow_scale_factor
  )

# 5. Calculate percentage variance explained for axis titles
var_explained <- round(100 * (pca_results$sdev^2 / sum(pca_results$sdev^2)), 1)

# 6. Plot the Biplot (Points + Arrows)
ggplot() +
  # Reference line grids
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray80") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray80") +
  
  # Layer A: The Data Points (drawn first so arrows stay on top)
  geom_point(
    data = df_pca_plot, 
    aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = any_detect, fill = any_detect, shape = cyano_present),
    size = 3, alpha = 0.6, stroke = 1
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("No" = "#154973", "Yes" = "#FACE00"), name = "Toxins Detected",
                     breaks = c("Yes", "No")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "#154973", "Yes" = "#FACE00"), name = "Toxins Detected",
                    breaks = c("Yes", "No")) +
 scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Cyanos Present",
    values = c("Yes" = 16, "No" = 17), # 16 = Filled Circle, 17 = Filled Triangle
    breaks = c("Yes", "No")
  ) +
  # Layer B: The Loading Arrows
  geom_segment(
    data = df_loadings,
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x_end, yend = y_end),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")),
    color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  
  # Layer C: The Parameter Labels
  # vjust/hjust adjustments prevent text from drawing directly on top of the arrow head
  geom_text_repel(
    data = df_loadings,
    aes(x = x_end, y = y_end, label = parameter),
    color = "black", fontface = "bold", size = 4, check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  
  labs(
    #title = "PCA Biplot of Water Parameters",
    #subtitle = "Points colored by toxin detection status; Red arrows indicate parameter loadings",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", var_explained[1], "% Variance Explained)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", var_explained[2], "% Variance Explained)")
  ) +
  theme_light() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )+
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.2)))+
  xlim(-5,9.5)


```
```{r random forest}
df_wide_complete<-df_wide |> 
  na.omit() |> 
  rename(chlorophyll_a = `chlorophyll-a`)

rf_fit<-ranger(
  formula = as.factor(any_detect) ~ ammonia+kjeldahl_nitrogen + chlorophyll_a+        
 nitrate_nitrite+total_phosphorus+dissolved_phosphorus+secchi_disk_depth+
   rdis_ix+rvegqc3oe+litcvrqc3oe+canopy_densiometer_percent,
  data = df_wide_complete, 
  importance = "permutation",
  probability = TRUE
)

print(rf_fit)

imp<-as.data.frame(importance(rf_fit))

df_results <- df_wide_complete %>%
  mutate(
    pred_prob_yes = rf_fit$predictions[, "Yes"],
    predicted_class = ifelse(pred_prob_yes > 0.5, "Yes", "No")
  ) %>%
  select(SITE_CODE, any_detect, pred_prob_yes, predicted_class) |> 
  mutate(prediction_true = case_when(
    any_detect == predicted_class ~ TRUE,
    any_detect != predicted_class ~ FALSE
  ))
```

```{r, comparing toxin detections across sample types}
toxins_sample_compare <- toxins2 %>%
  filter(PARAMETER_NAME %in% parameter_list) |>
  filter(SAMPLE_METHOD != "floating_mat") |> 
  group_by(SITE_CODE, PARAMETER_NAME, SAMPLE_METHOD) %>%
  summarize(
    any_detect = if_else(any(!is.na(RESULT_VALUE)), "Yes", "No")
  ) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = SAMPLE_METHOD, values_from = any_detect) |> 
  mutate(comparison = case_when(
    scrape %in% "Yes" & integrated_disturbance_sample %in% "No" ~ "scrape_not_ids",
    scrape %in% "Yes" & integrated_disturbance_sample %in% "Yes" ~ "scrape_and_ids",
    scrape %in% "No" & integrated_disturbance_sample %in% "Yes" ~ "ids_not_scrape",
    scrape %in% "No" & integrated_disturbance_sample %in% "No" ~ "none",
    .default = NA_character_
  ))
compare_summary<-toxins_sample_compare |> 
  group_by(PARAMETER_NAME) |> 
  count(comparison)

toxins2<-toxins2 |> 
  mutate(RESULT_VALUE = as.numeric(RESULT_VALUE))

toxins_samples_microcystin_scrapes<-toxins2 |> 
  filter(PARAMETER_NAME %in% "microcystin", SAMPLE_METHOD %in% "scrape") |>
```
